title: AWS CWI Training in Mobile, AL: 6-Day Exam Prep
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Mobile shipyard, steel, bridge and aerospace welders: D1.1, D1.5 or D1.2 for Part C. Corporate, online or one-to-one.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Mobile, Alabama: Six Days for Shipyard, Steel and Bridge Welding Inspectors
html:
Mobile builds ships, assembles airliners, rolls steel and has just started one of the largest bridge programs in the South. Austal USA's shipyard on the Mobile River, the Airbus campus at the Mobile Aeroplex at Brookley, ArcelorMittal's Calvert steelworks north of the city and the new I-10 Mobile River Bridge all depend on welding that somebody has to inspect and accept, and the credential that role usually calls for is the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI).

Atlantis NDT offers a six-day (6-day) course that prepares candidates for all three parts of the AWS examination: Part A Fundamentals, Part B Practical and Part C Code Application. It is available in corporate, online and one-to-one formats. AWS administers the exam and issues the certification; the course is preparation, and Atlantis does not certify anyone. There is no Atlantis classroom in Mobile. Atlantis has offices in Houston, Texas and Hyderabad, India, and Mobile Bay candidates use the formats described below. To discuss numbers or timing, send a Mobile CWI enquiry.

How the six days work for a Mobile candidate

Whichever format you choose, the content follows the same six blocks. Two days of fundamentals cover welding and cutting processes, standard terms, joint design, welding symbols, metallurgy, mechanical testing, discontinuities, NDT methods, safety, fabrication math and the inspector's role. One day prepares you for the practical, one is spent in your Part C code book, one is timed practice papers, and the last goes after the topics you missed. The AWS CWI course page sets out each block in detail.

  • Corporate suits a shipyard, module subcontractor, steel fabricator or plant maintenance contractor preparing a team. The six days are delivered at its own facility, with its welds, its gauges and, where it fits, its code and procedures.
  • Online suits an individual working shifts: a study plan built on the six-day outline, course materials, original practice questions and timed practice papers, with an instructor answering your questions as you go. No class times are scheduled; you choose when to study.
  • One-to-one suits a single candidate who wants direct tuition: six days of one-to-one sessions with the instructor, online or in person at a location agreed at booking.

The practice questions are Atlantis's own, written to the topic lists AWS publishes. They are not AWS examination questions, and AWS has not approved or endorsed the course.

Mobile's welding economy, sector by sector

Shipbuilding at Austal USA and around the bay

Austal USA employs about 3,000 shipbuilders in Mobile. For two decades the yard built all-aluminum ships, including the Navy's expeditionary fast transports and Independence-class littoral combat ships, and it has since moved largely to steel; in August 2026 its welders were at work on a Navy towing and salvage ship. The yard is also becoming part of the submarine supply chain. It outfits control room modules for Block V Virginia-class submarines that ship to General Dynamics Electric Boat, and a Navy-funded third module manufacturing facility is nearly finished, set to build several types of modules for Virginia- and Columbia-class boats. Austal has also signed Master Boat Builders to fabricate modules for Navy work, spreading the steel across more Gulf Coast yards.

Naval welding runs to NAVSEA technical publications and the Navy's own qualification and inspection requirements, not to an AWS code, and a CWI does not replace them. What the credential shows a yard QA manager is that an inspector understands processes, distortion, discontinuities, welding symbols and accurate measurement, which is why many shipyard inspectors go after it. Atlantis's marine work in the area is described on maritime NDT consulting in Mobile, with method detail on ultrasonic testing for marine work.

Aerospace at the Mobile Aeroplex at Brookley

Airbus opened its first A320 family final assembly line in Mobile in 2015 and inaugurated a second in October 2025. The campus also has an A220 line and employs more than 2,000 people. Final assembly joins large structures mostly by mechanical fastening, so fusion welding plays a small part in the airframe work itself; the welding sits in the supplier base, tooling, ground equipment and hangar construction around it. Inspectors working for aerospace suppliers can take AWS D17.1, the aerospace fusion welding specification, for Part C.

Steel at Calvert

North of the city, ArcelorMittal Calvert, now wholly owned by ArcelorMittal, makes flat-rolled steel and is building a plant for non-oriented electrical steel, the grade used in electric motors. Construction was continuing in mid-2026, with first production expected in the second half of 2027. A steelworks creates two kinds of welding inspection work: new construction of process lines, buildings and supports, mostly structural welding under AWS D1.1, and constant maintenance on cranes, rolls, chutes and mill equipment, where repair procedures, preheat and hardfacing matter as much as the code.

The I-10 Mobile River Bridge and Bayway

Construction of the I-10 Mobile River Bridge and Bayway program began in October 2026 under the Alabama Department of Transportation, with the Kiewit Massman Traylor team as design-builder. Phase one includes a six-lane cable-stayed bridge with a main span of about 2,575 feet and is scheduled to finish in late 2031; before work started, the team load-tested large steel pipe piles for the main pylons. A program of that size needs welding inspection for piling, for bridge steel fabricated under AWS D1.5, and for the approach and interchange work around it.

Port, process plants and pipelines

The Port of Mobile's terminals, the chemical and process plants along the river and across the county, and the pipelines that serve them add ASME piping and API 1104 work to the local mix. For owners who need vendor and field surveillance, Atlantis describes its services on third-party inspection in Mobile.

Who hires CWIs around Mobile, and what they look for

  • Shipyards and module builders. Yard QA departments want inspectors who understand fit-up, distortion control and visual acceptance on steel structure, and who can work comfortably with Navy documentation.
  • Bridge and civil contractors. The Mobile River program and state highway work create demand for inspectors who know D1.5, fabrication shop inspection and field welding of piles and connections.
  • Steel fabricators. Shops producing structural steel, platforms and equipment frames need in-house QC working to D1.1.
  • Mill and plant maintenance contractors. Repair-heavy work at the steelworks and process plants rewards inspectors who can check procedures, preheat and repair records rather than just the finished bead.
  • Aerospace suppliers. Companies feeding the Brookley campus and the wider Alabama aerospace sector need traceability and specification discipline.
  • Inspection firms. Third-party and source inspection for owners and for the naval supply chain.

Choosing a Part C code for Mobile work

For Part C you choose one code book from the AWS list: D1.1 structural steel, D1.2 aluminum, D1.5 bridges, D15.1 railcars, D17.1 aerospace, API 1104 pipelines, the ASME package (Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3) or the ISO option. Mobile's mix of yards, mills and civil work makes this choice more varied than in a refinery town.

Your workBook worth consideringReasoning
Steel ship structure, modules, fabrication shopsAWS D1.1The AWS code closest to yard structural work, and it transfers to other employers.
Aluminum vessels and structuresAWS D1.2For inspectors whose background is mainly aluminum, a skill set Mobile built up over two decades of aluminum ships.
Bridge steel, the I-10 programAWS D1.5The bridge welding code for state transportation steel.
Aerospace suppliersAWS D17.1Fusion welding for aerospace applications.
Process plant piping, steam and boiler workASME packageSection IX qualification with the B31.1 and B31.3 piping codes.
PipelinesAPI 1104Incorporated by federal pipeline safety rules.

Whichever book you pass, a Navy contract still brings its own specifications. Study the edition AWS names on your application, because exam editions often trail the newest printing. Useful background: AWS D1.1, the D1.1 acceptance criteria guide, AWS D1.5 and API 1104.

The AWS Mobile Section

The Mobile Section of AWS belongs to District 9 and meets regularly. In November 2024 it gathered at the AIDT Maritime Training Center, where Fronius presented on closing the welding skills gap to an audience of more than sixty. In March 2025 it hosted a joint section meeting in Spanish Fort attended by the AWS national president and the District 9 director, with a talk on welding certifications and an awards program.

Section meetings are the easiest place to meet yard QA managers and senior inspectors, hear how others prepared for the practical, and find supervisors willing to verify your experience for AWS. The current schedule is available through aws.org.

Where Mobile welders train

Mobile's training base grew up around shipbuilding. The AIDT Maritime Training Center on Addsco Road, run by Alabama's state workforce training agency and open since 2010, has 64 welding booths and teaches NCCER-based courses including structural welding, maritime structural fitting and maritime pipe fitting; it has trained workers for Austal. Bishop State Community College offers an associate degree, a certificate and short certificates in welding technology, including pipe welding, at its Carver campus, and in 2026 it ran a maritime boot camp. Shipyard apprenticeship programs add more welders every year.

For the CWI, that background counts. Completed trade or vocational courses lower the experience AWS asks for, and training records make your welding history easier to verify. These organizations have no connection with the Atlantis course; they appear here because they are where much of Mobile's welding workforce begins.

Booking the exam from Mobile

After AWS approves your application, its confirmation letter gives you an eligibility code. With it you schedule Part A (Fundamentals, 150 questions) and Part C (Code Application, roughly 50 to 65 questions with the book open) at a Prometric center; AWS puts the US count at more than 100. Part B, the practical, is run by AWS rather than Prometric: hands-on activities with tools and specimens it provides, plus 46 questions, at its own seminar and examination locations. Mobile candidates should check where AWS is holding practical sessions across the Gulf South and allow for travel if none is close. Each part requires at least 72%.

AWS sets and publishes its own fees on aws.org. The CWI exam cost guide helps you budget the rest, and the article on results by part explains where candidates struggle.

Studying around shipyard shifts and project milestones

Shipyards and mills work around the clock, and bridge and terminal projects have their own crunch points: pours, lifts, launches, sea trials. A study plan that depends on a fixed weekly class collapses the first time overtime is called. The online format avoids that. Spread the fundamentals over evenings and days off, keep a code book in your locker and look up the clause behind each joint you inspect, practise Part B measurements with a fillet gauge and a bridge cam gauge on scrap from the yard, and hold the timed papers back for the last stretch before your Prometric date. The instructor answers questions in writing whenever you send them. Gulf hurricane season, which runs from June to November, is worth planning around too; a storm can take a month out of anyone's calendar.

Corporate: six days at a Mobile shipyard, shop or plant

An employer with a group to prepare can host all six days at its own facility. A shipyard might use the course to build a bench of CWIs ahead of a new steel program, running the practical day on its own butt and fillet welds, stiffener connections and test coupons with its own gauges. A bridge fabricator might focus the code day on D1.5; a mill maintenance contractor might pair D1.1 with repair and hardfacing examples from its own jobs. Dates can be set around launches, outages and project milestones so key people are not pulled off critical work. Each candidate still applies to AWS individually, including the experience record and vision examination.

One-to-one: online or in person

Not everyone suits a self-paced plan. A long-serving welder stepping into a QC role, a supervisor whose new contract requires a CWI, or a candidate who missed one part and wants focused help can book six days of one-to-one sessions with the instructor. They can take place online or in person at a location agreed when booking. The outline is the same six days; the emphasis shifts to whatever you find hardest.

Eligibility and the vision record

Check eligibility before you start. AWS matches the years of welding-related experience to your education: five years with a high school diploma, one with a bachelor's degree in welding engineering or welding technology, four with completed trade or vocational courses, and longer with less schooling. See the full table on the CWI exam prep course page. Separately, AWS needs its Visual Acuity Record, showing near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more (glasses are fine) and a color perception test, signed by a qualified practitioner and recent enough for your exam. If the years are not there yet, the CAWI credential lets you inspect under a CWI's supervision while you build them; the CWI requirements guide covers both.

After the CWI: Mobile career paths

AWS keeps a CWI current for nine years, with renewal at the third and sixth years. In Mobile, shipyard inspectors often progress into QA supervision or toward the AWS Senior CWI (see the SCWI pathway), while bridge and mill inspectors add code endorsements.

Many also add nondestructive testing, particularly ultrasonic and magnetic particle testing for shipyard and structural work. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies its NDT staff through a written practice once training and method experience are in place, and Atlantis provides the training. Start with NDT training in Mobile, VT Level 2 and UT Level 2, and compare credentials on the CWI, API 577 and ASNT Level II page. Practical NDT in Mobile covers simulator-based practice. For local inspection services, see ultrasonic testing in Mobile, magnetic particle testing in Mobile and weld inspection.

Other Gulf South CWI pages, and your quote

Nearby candidates can compare the CWI exam prep pages for New Orleans, Birmingham, Tampa and Jacksonville.

When asking for a quote, include the number of candidates, the format each prefers (corporate, online or one-to-one), the code book each intends to use, and a brief note on their schooling and welding experience. For delivery at your premises, add the location, the gauges and sample welds you can supply, and any launch or outage dates to work around. Atlantis gives a quote on request rather than publishing fees; send the details through the Mobile CWI quote request.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in Mobile?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Mobile; Atlantis has offices in Houston and Hyderabad. Individuals study online with instructor support, employers can host the six days at their own facility, and single candidates can book one-to-one sessions online or in person. See the course outline.
AWS administers the CWI examination and issues the certification. Atlantis prepares candidates for it, and AWS has not approved, accredited or endorsed the course.

faq.q: I inspect at a shipyard building Navy vessels. Which Part C code should I take?
faq.a: Most steel yard inspectors choose AWS D1.1 because it is the AWS code closest to structural ship work. The Navy's own NAVSEA requirements still govern the ship, whichever book you pass.

faq.q: Is AWS D1.2 worth choosing if I came up on aluminum boats?
faq.a: It can be. D1.2 is the structural aluminum code, and inspectors with mainly aluminum experience sometimes find it the natural fit. If your future work is steel, D1.1 travels further.

faq.q: Will the I-10 Mobile River Bridge program need CWIs, and which code applies?
faq.a: Bridge steel for state transportation work is fabricated under AWS D1.5, the bridge welding code, which is a Part C option. See AWS D1.5.

faq.q: Where do Mobile candidates take the exam?
faq.a: Parts A and C are computer-based and booked at a Prometric center using the eligibility code in your AWS confirmation letter. Part B is run by AWS at its own seminar and examination locations, so check the schedule and allow for travel.

faq.q: Can a shipyard have the six days delivered at its facility?
faq.a: Yes. The corporate format brings the six days to your yard or shop, uses your gauges, welds and test coupons, and can be timed around launches and outages. Request a quote.

faq.q: Is one-to-one available online and in person?
faq.a: Yes. One-to-one gives a single candidate six days of sessions with the instructor, either online or in person at a location agreed when booking.

faq.q: Are the practice questions taken from AWS exams?
faq.a: No. Atlantis writes its practice questions from the AWS topic lists and has no access to the examination or its question bank.

faq.q: What can I add after the CWI?
faq.a: Common next steps are the AWS Senior CWI, code endorsements and NDT methods. Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training, after which your employer certifies you; see NDT training in Mobile.
